links.reason: 2016 has the women say பாவமிது and that a முதுபார்ப்பார் சாவர் தொடினே, so the guise 2008 chose (அந்தணாளனாய்ச் செல்லல் ... தெளிதாக உடைத்து) does what he reckoned. The later verse fulfils the plan and the note says how.

Both have the damned crying out, but 1930 says only that no one lifts them out and that they entered by their own earlier deeds (முந்தே வினைய முயன்றனர் புக்கார்); TM 165 says nothing about an answer. Deeds versus worship withheld are not incompatible, since not worshipping is itself a deed.
links.text_issue: TM 165: ஏழா நரகு and மாயன் are uncertain.

links.reason: Line 2 says earlier merit helps (புண்ணிய முன்னாட் செய்த போதந்தே யுதவி) and plans succeed; the vow follows, but the verse does not say the merit causes the vow. Kural 262 is தவம் to those who have தவம், not புண்ணியம் to a king; the circular rule is not shown working.

Both turn on feet: அடி பரவுவார்கட் கெளியானை and the claim that no one but the Lord may be counted god echo தாள்சேர்ந்தார்க் கல்லால். But the Kural already says only these, and 1906 adds no limit or condition, so it agrees rather than qualifies.

Both put the glance as a weapon (கடைக்கணித் துருவு காட்டினார் as Kaman's arrows; வேல்கண்ணள்), but 80 is young women taking the princes and NLD 17 warns a renunciant off another woman. The epic does not state or imply a limit, so the "teaches" is imported.

Line 4 இன்னதே is open: the wealth may be the fruit, or the fallen state. The kid's identity and the finding of doer by deed come from 197, not this verse, so neither teaches nor gains follows from 199 alone; the calf image is only loosely met.
links.text_issue: Line 4 இன்னதே ambiguous between wealth and fallen state.

links.reason: 280 has the king resolve என்றலை யரிந்தே ... சரணிடுவல்; 281 answers நின்னுயிரை நீகளையின் இன்னருள தென்னாம் and ties it to nourishing others' lives as one's own. The later verse refutes the earlier claim of atonement by head.

Both give bees humming பாலை (வண்டினம் பாலை முரல; வண்டினம் முரலும் நரம்பார்த் தன்ன ... வள்ளுயிர்ப் பாலை), in one a lover leading the girl on, in the other the spring that heralds parting. The pair does show the image taking its mood from the situation.

The subjects differ: 303 is the young Asvagriva, the enemy (அவ்விடை... குமாரகாலத்து), while 1512 is the hero who lifts the gem mountain. The note makes the boyhood feat the first form of the hero's strength, which joins two men.

2671 makes the king காமற்குங் காமனே among women skilled in song and dance; 1996 is Civakan's boast of Vimalai (வீடு பெற்றவரும் வீழும்). Neither answers, fulfils or reverses the other; "moves from one woman to many" is a theme, and the renunciation context is not in the verses.

Both name இருவினை, 365 burning them in meditation (தியானத்தி னிருவினை யெரித்து) and Kural 5 saying they do not cling to those devoted to the Lord's praise, so the cause of freedom differs. But the second gain overstates: the couplet does not say deeds end by devotion rather than meditation.

426 resolves to send an envoy; 590 reports the king speaking kindly and giving gifts. That is the plan carried out. The teaches rests on a silence and objection in 588-589, which are not in this packet or in 590.

Both set the evening as a wounding thing (மாலை புண்ணீரும் வேலிற் புகுந்தது; குழல்போலும் கொல்லும் படை). But in 2050 evening is the spear, not music, and the lover playing to a woman who has no lover is not in the verse.

NLD 84 asks the adulterer what pleasure he found, naming நீள்நிரயத் துன்பம்; 2769 has ஏதிலான் தார நம்பி made to embrace a red-hot copper image (செப்புப் பாவை) and cry out. The embrace itself becomes the torment, which the quatrain only names as hell.

2789 sends revilers and miserly sinners to animal births; 943 promises the dog a god's body by the mantra (நாயுடம் பிட்டு ... சேயுடம்). One is rule and the other a case of release by words, not an answer or fulfilment; "animal body is not final" is inferred, not stated.

Kural 557 likens the unkind king to a world without rain; Kalittokai 10 likens a withered waste to உலகு under கோல் கோடியவன் with men who rob and kill (கொலை அஞ்சா வினைவரால்). The same bond of bad rule and dry land is used in opposite directions.

1706 has the moon enter the queen's mouth (மதியந் தானே மடுத்தகம் அடைந்தது); 1730 has a gem reach the wife in a dream. Different objects; both are conception omens, a motif, and "parallel of Tivittan's own" is the marker's gloss only.

236 answers 234's சீவ னுண்டெனக் கண்ட தில்லை with fire that shows only on rubbing wood (விறகொடு விறகை யூன்ற ... அங்கி தோன்றி). The reply is by method, as the note says, and the later verse refutes the earlier.

Both dreams have a man take the woman off (போய்ஓர் பெரும்பதியுள்; கொண்டு போம்), but one is read as marriage by experts and the other is told by Kannaki to a friend; a dream foretelling is a convention, not a shared distinctive image. SP is not "read by others".

1706 argues from ornaments: if he were dead வெள்வளை முத்த நீக்கி; 351 has Vijayai breaking bangles and removing rings. The custom is real, but 1706 states it generally and does not use Vijayai's scene.

1970 denies soul, rebirth and good and ill (இல்லையுயி ரென்று); TM 2558 sends those who say there is no higher state (பரகதி) to hell. The denials differ, so the second gain fails; both are only a bad end for a denier.

1839 says wealth and gods' pleasure are வினையதனின் விளைவு; 1842 has Payapati say pleasure is fruit of swollen merit and வித்திடற் பால, more to sow. The advice is applied and the king adds the step of sowing.

Both prophecies are spoken by சுமித்திர முனி (272 to Naravahanan, 282 to Nilavekan), so "one sage ... another" is false. They do fit one destiny (Vellimalai realm; bride and earth), but the note's contrast of sources fails.

354 foretells a king who gives up rule becomes lord of gods for seventeen oceans; 560 gives the renouncer who takes கேவலப் பெண் and becomes அமரர்க்கு மரியன். The second shows a fruit beyond godship, which limits what 354 holds.

NLD 121 says the meat-eater's வயிறு is a காடு for beasts and birds; Neelakesi 32 only describes a shrine among pyres with demons eating bodies. Nothing in 32 stages the quatrain's metaphor; the pair shares the word for burning ground.
Both give light: அணிவான்சுடராகி நின்றான் and தருமச் சுடரான். சுடர் is the common epithet for a Jina, so the shared image is conventional and the "where he stands / what he teaches" split is thin.

2173 reverses 2168: வலக்கண்கள் துடித்த for the women against இறைவன் கண்வல னாடிற்று, and கொற்ற முரசம் பாடவிந்து against the roaring drums. The same sign takes opposite value by side and by sex, as the note says.

Both poems have a heart pressed to go for wealth through a killing waste. 327 does not weigh a man by what he carries (கொன்றோர் கோல்கழிபு இரங்கும்), so the road "weighing life by cargo" is only 337. 337 does not develop 327.
1571 states a rule for gifts (வேதியர்க் கல்லால் ஈத லில்லை) and Kural 134 ranks conduct above Veda. The jester "passing neither" is not in the verse, so both claims of the note and its gains fail.

Saccandan vouches by love and past wins (என் அலால் பிறரை இல்லான்; மொய் அமர் பலவும் வென்றான்) and bars further words, with no test for rule; Kural 509 says தேறற்க ... தேராது. The verse shows trust resting on service rather than examination of fitness.

2727 observes மெலியவர் பெற்ற செல்வம் ... வலியவர் கொண்டு and chooses penance; Kural 250 tells the strong to remember their own fear. The verse is no rule against oppression and shows no ruler moved by it, so "answers the warning" and both gains are the note's.

458 has men say the hair burns and the eyes kill (நெடுங்கணிவை வல்லகொலை) and worship; NLD 44 refuses such talk of eyes as வேல்/கயல், calling the speakers கண்ணில் புன் மாக்கள் and the eye a scooped palm fruit. The image works only on one who consents to be struck.

130 gives a golden city on the southern ridge; 535 compares the city to Indra's gem casket opened. The images differ and only the topic (a Vidyadhara city) is shared; "genre convention" is not shown by two verses.

520 promises restoration வஞ்சமொன் றின்றி; 574 says the whole wreck was வஞ்சம். The pun and the reveal are real, but the claims do not conflict, since the promise is kept; it is irony and a later reveal, not a tension.

1962 lists flesh-sellers, crushers and hunters and says the beasts' pain never lets up (விடலில வேதனை), but names no rebirth as the beast or reckoning; Siddhar 269 has Death bite back. The note's "implies birth as the beast he hunted" is not in the verse.

37 has the queen ask நற்றவமு மாமோ and the sage promise a son; Kural 70 sets a son and the father's நோற்றான். Both link son and tapas in the same direction, so "reverses" is false; the verse's own sense is uncertain.
links.text_issue: Sense of நற்றவம் ஆமோ is open.

links.reason: 2841 says the middle gift pays out by wishing trees (தானமிடையது செய்த நீரார்); Kural 222 says giving is good even if there is no higher world. The contrast of reward and no reward is real but the claims are not incompatible, so tension does not fit.

1383 line 4 ஊனுடம் பிதன்பொருட் டுடையல் வேண்டுமோ may be a taunt or doubt about the body; the note builds on the taunt reading. Kural 969's dying for honour needs more than மானமில் லிர்காள், so the "rule hurled at cowards" gain is conjecture.
links.text_issue: Last two lines turn on a rare construction.

links.reason: 318 gives the ascetics' arrival (போதவிழ் பொழில் புகுந்திருந்தனர்); 323 shows the leader preaching. This is story order, and 318 does not say they came to teach, so the link adds only sequence.

685 has the king see the dancer's longing for Civakan and take her by force (செற்றம்); 1262 has the king see the same look and call him (காதலிற் களித்தது). A deliberate echo with opposite response, but it is a contrast of scenes, not incompatible claims.

203 has Kattiyankaran take the yoke (படு நுகம் பூண்பல்); 2147 has him pledge life and call Govindan lord (இனி யிறைவன் றானே). The echo is of a treacherous pledge, not a tension of claims, and "word for word" overstates.

2556 says wealth does not come without fortune (திருமுயங்க லில்லையெனின் இல்லை பொருளீட்டம்) and may come home to one who goes not a cubit; Kural 376 says what is one's own stays. The turn to தவம் in line 4 is the epic's addition but rests on a hard reading.

Both use கொன்று ... கொணர (1080 கொன்றுயிர் கொணர; SP 153 கொன்றச் சிலம்பு கொணர்க), a common formula. The unexamined order, Civakan's submission and the god who intervenes are not in 1080, so the contrast is the note's.

126 lists what desire ruins in the doer (மானத் திண்மை, புகழ், கண்ணொடு கலக்கும்); 216 is leprosy (அழுகி நைந்து ... புண்ணின் உருவினள்). Nothing in 216 shows desire wasting the body or the resolve "borne out"; the link is a stretched theme.
